STEP 1 - Scene: A single cookie (looks like a dark chocolate chip cookie with a few light chips or nut pieces) on a white square plate, photographed from above at roughly a top-down angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The square white plate is about 24 cm across its width. Vessel area ≈ 24 x 24 x ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 490 cm^2. Using a round-equivalent of ~24 cm diameter gives 3.14 x 12^2 ≈ 452 cm^2; I use ~470 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: one chocolate chip cookie.

STEP 4 - Area: The cookie is roughly 6.5 cm in diameter, so about 33 cm^2, which is about 7% of the plate area.

STEP 5 - Volume: A cookie of this size is about 1.2 cm thick. 33 cm^2 x 1.2 cm ≈ 40 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Baked cookie density is close to 0.9-1.0 g/ml when dense, but cookies are airy, so I use about 0.9 g/ml for a dense cookie envelope: 40 ml x 0.9 ≈ 36 g. A typical chocolate chip cookie of this diameter weighs roughly 30-40 g, which agrees.

STEP 7 - Energy: Chocolate chip cookies are about 480 kcal per 100 g. 36 g x 4.8 ≈ 173 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One medium cookie on a large plate, about 36 g and about 170 kcal, is plausible. The plate is mostly empty, so the total is small.

Total: about 36 g, about 173 kcal.
